correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<d<2 the swapped positive unit pair x=((2+d)/4,(2−d)/4), y with coordinates reversed has distance d and identical first derivatives of norm under every complex z, yielding upper coefficient d/(1−d²/4) by imaginary-direction quadratic curvature. For arbitrary near-minimizing pairs with B(x,y;a)=O(a²), compactness in real dimension four rules out a vanishing limit coordinate (symmetric increments H(u,w) would diverge on a² scale, or distinct phases on the other coordinate cost O(a)). The first-order perturbation forces coordinatewise phase agreement; symmetric transverse variations force each curvature gap |1/r_j−1/s_j|/2. The monotone two-denominator minimax over radii with total separation ≥d uniquely balances swapped coordinates and attains d/(1−d²/4). Thus the limit and asymptotic rigidity follow without finite extrapolation. Independent direct transverse evaluations at d=.2,1,1.7 and a=.01,.001 converge to exact coefficient.
